newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn sees no sign of early stability pact deal.
newsitem.headline: Quinn sees no sign of early stability pact deal.

text.p: Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn, set to chair a special European Union finance ministers' meeting, said on Thursday he had no reason to believe a deal was imminent on the EU row over a post-EMU stability pact.
Asked whether he believed that proposals made by the European Commission would be enough to prompt a deal, he said, 'I have no prior indication that we can anticipate a breakthrough.'
Quinn was arriving for the meeting of EU finance ministers, aimed at thrashing out differences over the pact before a two-day summit of EU heads of government.

Asked where the disagreement lay over the pact, meant to enforce fiscal discipline after EU states launch a single currency in 1999, Quinn said the problem was how to define the exceptional circumstances in which states would be escape fines for exceeding a budget deficit limit of three percent.
Germany is pushing for a strict definition of a two percent fall in economic growth, while other states were seeking a range between 0.5 and 2.0 percent.
